content.text: The first postcondition is wrong: it asks for `v <= |s[i]| - 1`, but `v` equals the length of some element, so it can never hold. It should be `v <= |s[i]|`.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "ensures",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The first postcondition requires v <= |s[i]| - 1 for every i, i.e. v strictly smaller than every list length. But v is the minimum length and equals |s[k]| for some k (second postcondition / invariant), so v <= |s[k]| - 1 is impossible. The loop invariant (v <= |s[k]| for all k < i) plus exit i == |s| gives only v <= |s[i]|, so the bridge to the postcondition fails. Fix: ensures v <= |s[i]|."}
EOF
sed -i 's/v <= (|s\[i\]|) - 1/v <= |s[i]|/' program.dfy && sed -n 3p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
I fixed the first postcondition in `program.dfy`, and Dafny now verifies the file (2 verified, 0 errors).

**What was wrong:** The first postcondition said `v <= |s[i]| - 1` for every `i`, meaning `v` had to be strictly smaller than every list's length. But `v` is the shortest length, so it equals `|s[k]|` for some `k` (the second postcondition says exactly this). That would require `|s[k]| <= |s[k]| - 1`, which is impossible. When the loop ends, the invariant only gives `v <= |s[k]|` for all `k`, so the step from the invariant to the postcondition (the "bridge" check) failed.

**Fix:** I changed line 3 to `ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> v <= |s[i]|`, which is what "smallest list length" means. The method body and loop invariants are unchanged.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before editing: the failing element is `ensures` and the obligation is `bridge`.
